note: Derived reading aid. Never authoritative; never read as intent (Decision 0004). The Plan document governs.
author: Lightweight model draft for Clara (technical writing) via Claudia Atlas <claudia.atlas@agents.arcadia.local>
title: Show what a project is and how it got here
purpose: Gives each Arcadia-managed project a readable map of its living system and a timeline of how it changed. Each entry links back to its source and proof, and no long documentation is needed first.
serves: The Project outcome of the operator understanding the portfolio without holding it all in mind.
done_when: A project's map and timeline can be generated at no cost, and each entry links back to the record it came from.

actions.title: Define how a project describes its living system
actions.why: Gives every project one shared format for its purpose, topics and relationships.
actions.done_when: A project can declare its topics, relationships and views in one standard file, with each topic tied to repository sources.

actions.title: Derive the project's story from Arcadia records
actions.why: Builds the timeline and status from records Arcadia already holds, not from new writing.
actions.done_when: The timeline groups related Actions, keeps unlinked log entries visible, and each status item names its source.

actions.title: Write the map and timeline into the Obsidian vault
actions.why: Gives the operator readable notes for each project in the vault they already use.
actions.done_when: The projector writes map, timeline and topic notes only under the project's own folder, and leaves other vault areas untouched.

actions.title: Refresh living-system notes as a normal command
actions.why: Keeps the notes current without a model or a paid service.
actions.done_when: A preview shows every create, update and skip without writing, and applying writes exactly what was previewed.

actions.title: Prove the approach on Arcadia and a second project
actions.why: Shows the approach works on real projects, not only on a test fixture.
actions.done_when: Both projects' descriptions explain their own workflow, and their timelines show pauses and resumptions without rewriting history.
